payload.summary: The pinned repo is the official ROCKET code (Dempster, Petitjean and Webb). The claim maps to code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py. For each dataset it loads the fixed UCR _TRAIN.txt and _TEST.txt split. It then runs num_runs (default 10) times, each with a fresh generate_kernels(input_length, 10_000) and apply_kernels. It fits RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=np.logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True) and records classifier.score on the test set. It saves accuracy_mean and accuracy_standard_deviation to results_ucr.csv. ECG200 is among the bake-off datasets. The repo has no dataset-name txt files, so the user must create a one-line file containing ECG200. The ECG200 data is not in the repo. There is no requirements file, and the README only lists Python, Numba, NumPy and scikit-learn (or equivalent).

entrypoints.why: Official UCR script. It does 10 runs by default with 10,000 kernels, using the fixed train/test split, RidgeClassifierCV, and mean test accuracy per dataset. Run it with a dataset-names file that lists ECG200.
Older preprint-era version that loops over all 85 bake-off datasets, including ECG200, with no dataset-list argument. It uses the deprecated np.int. It is an alternative, not the primary entry point.
Core ROCKET implementation (generate_kernels and apply_kernels, numba-jitted), imported by the scripts.

dataFiles.why: Not in the repo. They come from the timeseriesclassification.com Univariate2018 archive (txt/arff version) or the UCR archive. The script expects the layout {input_path}/{name}/{name}_TRAIN.txt, with the label in column 0.
Repo-provided results for the train/test split across datasets. I did not read it, so as not to see the values.
Resample results. This is not the fixed split, so it is not the target.

metricSources.description: _results[i] = classifier.score(X_test_transform, Y_test) per run. results.loc[dataset,'accuracy_mean'] = _results.mean(), written to {output_path}/results_ucr.csv. The script does not print the accuracy; it only writes the CSV.
Authors' stored results for comparison. I did not open it.

payload.runInstructions:
1. Install numba, numpy, pandas and scikit-learn. The scripts use RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=True), and `normalize` was removed in scikit-learn 1.2. Use scikit-learn <1.2 (e.g. 1.1.x) with a compatible numpy and numba. Also, np.NINF in rocket_functions.py was removed in NumPy 2.0, so use numpy <2.
2. Download the UCR ECG200 txt files and place them at ./Univariate_arff/ECG200/ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200_TEST.txt.
3. Create a file ecg200.txt that contains the single line ECG200.
4. cd code && python reproduce_experiments_ucr.py -d ../ecg200.txt -i ../Univariate_arff -o ./
5. Read accuracy_mean for ECG200 in ./results_ucr.csv. The defaults are -n 10 and -k 10000.
warnings: The repo has no requirements or lock file, and dependency_discover found none. Versions are unpinned.
normalize=True in RidgeClassifierCV fails on scikit-learn >=1.2. np.NINF fails on NumPy >=2.0. Pin older versions or make a minimal compatibility edit.
The kernels are drawn from numba's np.random without a seed, so the 10-run mean will vary slightly between executions.
The dataset is not bundled, and the repo has no bakeoff.txt names file. You need to supply both.
The script writes results only to the CSV and prints no accuracy.
The .preprint scripts are older. The bake-off one uses np.int, which fails on newer NumPy.
I did not open the stored results CSVs, in keeping with the blinding.

payload.summary: Run the reviewed single-dataset adapter rocket-ecg200-runner. It imports the pinned repo's code/rocket_functions.py (generate_kernels and apply_kernels). It loads the fixed UCR ECG200 train and test txt files and does 10 runs. Each run draws fresh 10,000 random kernels and fits RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True) on the training set. It scores each run on the test set and writes metrics.accuracyMean (the mean of the 10 test accuracies, as a fraction) to artifacts/result.json. The adapter is needed because the official script code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py fails on a one-row dataset-name file: np.loadtxt returns a scalar for it. The pinned requirements are used unchanged, with scikit-learn 1.1.3 because normalize=True was removed in 1.2, and numpy below 2 because of np.NINF. The dependency_check reports binary wheels are available for all seven pinned requirements on Python 3.11, linux/arm64. The dataset is the reviewed ECG200.zip download, extracted, with the sha256 from the reviewed source.
stopConditions: Stop if the dependency install fails or the pinned wheels cannot be installed.
Stop if the ECG200 archive hash does not match the reviewed sha256, or ECG200_TRAIN.txt or ECG200_TEST.txt is missing.
Stop if the adapter errors, for example a TypeError from RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=...) because the scikit-learn version is wrong.
Stop if artifacts/result.json is not written or lacks metrics.accuracyMean.
Stop if the run exceeds the 900 s command timeout.
risks: The adapter is project-owned, not official repository code. It reproduces the loop of the official script for ECG200 only and imports the authors' rocket_functions.py.
Kernels are drawn from numba's unseeded np.random, so the 10-run mean will vary between executions. The paper does not state a seed.
The paper states no preprocessing, and the code applies none. The raw txt values are used as given.

The paths for the extracted dataset (../work/data/ECG200_*.txt) and for the output (../artifacts/result.json, relative to cwd repo) are my assumptions about the lab layout. I found no board evidence confirming them, so they may need adjusting to where the lab places the extracted files.
The official script was not run directly, because it fails on a one-row dataset-name file and does not print accuracy.
